content:
Jon Stewart on Wednesday ripped those fixating on disgraced ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s affair with an alleged Chinese spy and not the scandal involving the company and President Donald Trump’s administration.

When Huang stepped down last week, his defenders protested that his resignation would harm the U.S. in its AI race with China. (The chair of Nvidia’s board stated earlier this week that it has no plans to reinstate Huang.)

“We all focus on, you know, infidelity and the sensationalism,” Stewart said on his “Weekly Show” podcast. “But the larger issue is, we’ve been told you cannot say anything to these guys, you cannot slow their roll, you cannot possibly stand in the way. Because if you do, China will rule the future.”

“Meanwhile,” he added, “this fucking guy [Huang], with the help of [Commerce Secretary] Howard Lutnick and Donald Trump, were siphoning our best chips to China for a profit that Lutnick’s sons’ company got a piece of. And Trump’s stock in that company soared.”

After joining Trump’s Cabinet last year, Lutnick handed control of his investment firm Cantor Fitzgerald to his sons. Per CNBC’s reporting, the firm held a roughly $1.2 billion stake in Nvidia when Lutnick was confirmed to the Cabinet post in January 2025, raising conflict-of-interest concerns.

Trump reportedly held tens of millions of dollars in Nvidia stock as recently as August of this year.

On Wednesday, House Democrats launched an investigation into whether Lutnick’s family’s financial ties to Nvidia played a role in his alleged resistance to implementing export controls on Megaspeed, the Singaporean company run by Jensen Huang’s mistress, alleged spy Alice Huang.

Stewart’s producer Gillian Spear remarked that the “best case” scenario for the disgraced Nvidia executive was “unknowingly sleeping with a spy,” while the “worst case” was that he was “intentionally circumnavigating U.S. export controls to enrich our president and his secretary.”

“Whether he knew she was a spy, didn’t know she was a spy, doesn’t even matter,” Stewart said.

“As a matter of fact, let’s say he just knew her and wasn’t sleeping with her. The business that they were doing with Megaspeed of smuggling those chips to China should be enough to disqualify him, having nothing to do with any of the other shenanigans.”
